subject: HelixGuard regional throughput storm — emergency cross-region reroute and executive briefing
messages:
From: Dana Morales <dana@helixguard.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: sustained 5xx + latency affecting us-east-1 (HelixGuard)

Marissa —

We're seeing a severe spike across our API gateways to your us-east-1 AZ cluster starting ~07:50 PDT. We're experiencing sustained 5xx at ~15% and p95 latency jumping from 220ms to ~1.6s. This is impacting our ingestion pipeline and realtime scoring — customers are seeing failures.

We've attached a short error snapshot and dashboard. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a regional capacity/regression issue or a routing problem? We need immediate mitigation and an ETA for a cross-region fallback.

Dana Morales
Head of Platform, HelixGuard
Dana Morales | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: error-snapshot-logs.tar.gz (log bundle), kpi-dashboard.png (screenshot)

Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: sustained 5xx + latency affecting us-east-1 (HelixGuard)

Team — looping you in. Customer reports sustained 5xx and p95 latency spike in us-east-1 AZ. Dana indicates impact to ingestion/scoring and requests an immediate cross-region fallback and ETA.

Immediate asks:
- Can SRE confirm whether this is capacity or a routing spike (KV cache pressure vs. noisy host)?
- Recommend fallback target region (us-west-2 or central)?
- Sales / CS: what concession/credit should we offer if it's >2 hours?

I want a short exec-bridge in 30 min if we have nontrivial action.

Marissa Cole

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: sustained 5xx + latency affecting us-east-1 (HelixGuard)

Marissa — quick triage:
- Initial SRE notes: spike correlates with surges to a small subset of host pools in us-east-1; KV cache eviction rates are abnormally high and we're seeing tokenization-related hot keys. Not a control-plane outage.
- Recommended mitigation: immediate regional traffic redistribution to us-west-2 for write-heavy ingestion endpoints; keep read+inference pinned to us-east-1 for consistency where possible.
- Action plan we can execute within 25 mins: 1) Gradual traffic steer at lb-level (20% -> 50% -> 100% over ~15–20m) to us-west-2, 2) Warmed instance pool in west, 3) Enable prefix KV stabilization for their hot keys.

I will open the exec bridge and post the join link. Karthik — can you validate capacity in us-west-2 for their committed qps and burst headroom?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Outbound & Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: sustained 5xx + latency affecting us-east-1 (HelixGuard)

Confirmed capacity: us-west-2 has warm reserved pools that can absorb HelixGuard's steady-state and up to 2.5x burst. No quota blockers.
I will initiate the traffic steer once SRE confirms the green on KV stabilization tasks. We should also prepare a temporary config pin (session affinity TTL) for scoring endpoints to reduce cold starts during the steer.

Attachment: reroute-plan-v1.pdf (planned steps & rollback checklist)

Karthik Iyer
Principal Site Reliability Engineer

Marissa / Sean — thank you for the quick response.

We need the reroute now. Our legal/procurement team will need a timeline for impact and a note on credits for customer SLA exposure (we have paying customers that had failed calls this morning). If the steer will take 20–30 minutes, confirm so we can update our operations channel and start throttling nonessential workloads.

Dana

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 31 Jul 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: HelixGuard regional throughput storm — emergency cross-region reroute and executive briefing

Dana & team —

Status update and executive summary:
- Timeline: We initiated rolling traffic redistribution to us-west-2 at 2028-07-30T09:10:00-07:00. Full diversion for ingestion endpoints completed by 09:30 PDT.
- Impact: 5xx reduced from 15% -> <1.5% within 22 minutes of the final step. p95 latency returned to ~240ms for the steered endpoints. Some inference paths remained on us-east-1 to avoid session divergence; those were <3% error rate.
- Root cause: transient KV cache thrash combined with hot prefix amplification in a small host subset. Engineering has applied KV stabilization and hot-key mitigation; long-term options include prefix replication and a tuned session affinity for scoring endpoints.
- Compensation: As an immediate gesture for customer impact, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of July usage for HelixGuard, pending procurement confirmation. For repeated events or SLA miss > 2 hours, we'll escalate credit to contract terms per the SLA.
- Next steps:
  1) Postmortem to be shared within 72 hours (engineering lead: Karthik Iyer).
  2) Joint workshop to discuss cache replication and routing policy by Aug 10.
  3) Internal: run a korrelate report on hot-prefix patterns for HelixGuard (SRE).

We appreciate the patience and the quick coordination from your ops team. I will schedule a 30-minute executive bridge for Thursday 09:00 PDT to review the postmortem draft and next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec — Customer Success Escalations
Redwood Inference
